Hi Ed,

 

When using summary, there's only one slot for a chi-square so that's all we report (the Mplus chi-square in that case. To see all the chi-square values try using inspect(fit, "impute"). 

 

One note on the output. The results from the ML and LMRR fit statistics are F statistics. To convert to a chi-square, multiply the F value by the model df.

 

Alex

 

P. S. I'm very aware of the issues surrounding missing data in any number of fields. A perceived barrier to modern methods of handling missing data is that they are perceived to be too "hard" for many applied researchers to learn. One of our goals with runMI was to provide a straightforward implementation of MI using SEM. The more tools like this we have the better adoption will be (I hope!).

On Friday, October 10, 2014 10:26:20 AM UTC-4, Edward Rigdon wrote:

     I was demonstrating missing data procedures for my class this week.  Of course, I demo’ed the FIML option in lavaan, but I also wanted to demo multiple imputation via runMI.  The documentation, as I understand it, says that the chi=”all” option will produce multiple chi-squares, based on different approaches to combining across imputations.  But when I run it (see attached transcript and attached synthetic dataset), I only get one chi-square.  Am I misunderstanding the documentation, or am I doing something wrong?

     Sadly, the very notion of missing data procedures beyond pairwise deletion or mean-plugging (ick!) was a revelation to this class of business Ph.D. students, who have been through several quant methods courses before they get to mine.  Somewhere, the word is not getting out that there are better solutions.

     Thanks.

--Ed Rigdon
